Hit the freeze pop-up to freeze the ball in place for a short time. When the whole playing field is "painted" you can move to the next level.

211888.overview: Remake of the 1982 Konami arcade game Pooyan. There is another Amiga remake called Struggle, also published in 1991. You play a pig who goes up and down a pole, as hungry wolves attack from the left, and float down with balloons

211902.overview:
Simplified version of the Licenseware game Paradox from the same author. Pollymorph is a single-player colour-matching puzzle game.

In this game the player controls a small ball that can be used move other balls around. When two same-coloured balls meet they disappear and the game objective is to clear the game area by pushing balls of the same colour together.

The number of balls and the complexity of the game area increases as the player progresses through the game.

211953.overview: Released as part of the classic compilation: Gamers' Delight 2. Graphics and gameplay are virtually identical to Mean Arenas  The player and enemy sprites were ripped from Space Crusade  Most of the original sounds were replaced. Not sure about the sources.

211954.overview: The standard Pac-Man gameplay was changed in this version. A level does not fit onto one screen. Instead, the screen scrolls. You don't have an overview of where the ghosts are at all times. Now they can surprise you, coming from angles you did not have a view of. To compensate, they do not seem to chase you as actively as they do in other versions of Pac-Man. Part of the classic collection: Gamers' Delight 2.

211955.overview:
Fun little game similar to the Pengo games. You must push blocks to kill the enemies and such small levels produce nerves! It's an original concept.

At least 3 versions of this game exists. The only difference between the versions seems to be in which order the levels appears.

211956.overview: Arkanoid / Breakout clone that is a sequel to Walls and was part of the classic collection: Gamers' Delight 2..

211982.overview:
Pong for up to four players with objects in the middle that can affect the ball's movement. Four-player mode sounds exciting at first, but it does not really work in my opinion: If, for example, you play on the top side and the ball gets deflected to the top by either the player on the left or the player on the right, the distance can be so short you simply do not have enough time to react.

2x2 - two players are positioned at the top and two at the bottom of the screen. They play in co-op mode and their points are added up. The first team; top or bottom, who reach 21 points wins.
At the start only two players are initialised. The other two players will appear if they press fire to join. If all 4 players join, a second ball will be added.

4x4 - each player is positioned at his own side of the screen. 1 point goes to the player that was last to hit the ball before it went out of the screen. -1 point goes to the player in front of the side of the screen where the ball went out. Points don't go below zero. The winner is the first one who reaches 10 points.

Both types of the game start with a 3 second countdown. Unless a player hits fire, the player is controlled by CPU. You can either press fire during the countdown or join the game later. There's gravity towards the centre of the screen which is unnoticeable at the start but slowly increases.

The Eye is revolving in random directions around the center of the screen and can also bounce the ball. It slowly aproaches the center of the screen and gravity gets stronger until it's caught at the center. It's satellite, if picked up by the ball it acts like power-up / down.

Black satellite - turns off the screen for a second.
Red satellite - slows down all players for 5 seconds except the one who last to hit the ball before it collided with the Eye's satellite.
Blue Satellite - freezes all players for 3 seconds except the one who last to hit the ball before it collided with the Eye's satellite.

211990.overview: Amiga shareware game.It's based in an old Spectrum game.. Stop the paratroopers before they get to the ground. Take out 40 planes to move to the next level. Your final score is based on the number of bullets you have left at the end of each level, the number of paratroopers you have hit, a bonus depending on the proportion of aircraft hit and a bonus if you hit all the paras.

212013.overview:
The idea with Particle Man is to collect and dispose of a number of bombs which are placed in the maze at random by the monsters. The bombs have a limited life and if left alone for too long will explode. If this happens, Particle Man loses some energy and if all his energy is lost he loses a life. A collision with any of the monsters also results in a lost life. As a warning, when a bomb's timer is below the half-way stage, it will flash. 
 
To dispose of a bomb you must absorb it. If the bombs are close together, run over the one you want an press fire. If far apart PM will absorb the first bomb he encounters. Once absorbed PM can dispose of the bomb by running over a portal.

The game could be best described as somewhat of a reverse Bomber Man.

212014.overview: This game, a bit of an R-Type clone, with source code was released as part of AMOS Pro as a learning example for AMAL, BLOBS and collisions.

212015.overview: A cool Pac-Man and platformer mashup game from the golden era of Amiga gaming. A very playable game. Some people have recently released this game as Platman Worlds (2017) on the C64, with 4 worlds instead of just one, so anyone who loved the Amiga game can check that out for an almost identical challenge on the C64.

212016.overview:
It is a top-down game where players sit on floats, trying to sink the other players by throwing sea urchins at them. "Plouf!" is the French onomatopoeia for the sound made by an object when it falls into a liquid.

You control your float like an RC car: you can accelerate, slow down and rotate left or right. The islands on the screen are randomly generated, so each game looks different.

212020.overview: An updated version of the classic Pong game, a true classic from the golden era gaming with enough twists and updates to make it all interesting without changing the overall flavor of the game.

212021.overview: Push 'n' Shove is an Amiga puzzle brain game released in 1995. A Sokoban clone with elements borrowed from other games.

212026.overview: Game deliberately made in the style of an 8-bit game, for some imaginary 8-bit machine. Except the music, which was a placeholder for some suitably bleepy chip tune. The aim of this game while playing as a Cat is to eat all the mice in a level before moving onto the next through each exit door. Be careful though as throughout each level there are dogs that if touched will kill you and you will lose a life. However PuzCat isn't weak and can push blocks to squash the dogs or enable you to jump over them when properly placed.

212082.overview:
Yet another Pac-Man clone. This one is quite good actually. I kinda like that you can change the music during playing. Also the funny animations that plays every fourth level are cool.  Game design by Andreas Oberdorfer; level design by Michael Gehmair. 68K Coding by Andreas Oberdorfer; RTG support (68K/OS4) & AmigaOS4 port by Jürgen Schober. Graphics by Andreas Oberdorfer; high score image by Christopher Dissauer; fruits, animation & scanning by Thomas Kutschera. Music by Andreas Oberdorfer; popman.mod based on an original composition (popcorn.mod) by Hawk/Atomic in 1988. 
 
Game includes a built-in level editor allowing players to create their own levels (or modify existing levels), and features full multitasking (memory permitting), joystick/joypad/keyboard support and WB window gameplay (256 colours only).

212083.overview: The Sequel to Parasite from Shaun Watters and Tim Gilbert. A 2D RPG dungeon crawler.

212084.overview: Matching pairs, puzzle game for 1 to 2 players with good graphics, decent background music and no sound effects. There are different tile sets to choose from: one abstract and stylish, another cartoony. Magazine publisher 1: Amiga Fun (UK) no. 6, Apr 1991. Magazine publisher 2: Amiga Fun (Germany)

212085.overview:
The Pixie Kingdom is an Amiga labyrinth/maze arcade game. The evil leader Nogrim has invaded the Pixie Kingdom and is holding them prisoner in their own city! One pixie escaped and  now asks you to return and rescue the innocent pixies...
You set off immediately with sword in hand to face whatever Nogrim might throw at you!
Fight if you must, find the keys and take the pixies to the exit.

212086.overview:
You have been accidentally turned into a fish, now you must make your way through several underwater screens in search of the ancient Posiden, only he can change you back to a human. The underwater worlds contains numerous dangers you must avoid. Eat enough small fish and you move to the
next level.

212087.overview: Project Battlefield is a timed FPP shooter with a main character modelled after Robocop. As a cybernetic police officer the player will face five stages of fight against terrorists and robots, occupying government buildings. Some places may be reached by using teleports, others require the player to find a proper access card or a hidden passage switch. The player may use some objects as shields, such as barrels and containers. The screen size can be adjusted depending on the Amiga power.

212088.overview:
Unofficial conversion and upgrade based on the ZX Spectrum game. Growing the best Thyrgodian Megga Chrisanthodil possible is the sole purpose of Robbie the Robot. When insects invade his garden, he has to stop them ruining his work. He has a canister of insect repellent, a smoke-bomb and a startling streamer, each placed on walls at the side of his garden. Each will stun any particular vermin, but you will need to find out exactly what kills what.

As the plant grows, aided by the timely addition of compost bags, leaves will start to shoot outwards. The more leaves there are, the quicker it will grow (a simple incorporation of the concept of photosynthesis being boosted by having more sunlight absorbed), so don't let the bugs near it - those whose programmed movement path takes them towards an existing leaf should be your priority. Once the plant is high enough, it flowers and you move onto another level, where increasingly tough foes are on the prowl.

212089.overview: A puzzle game where you slowly reveal the picture hidden below. The game does have it's fair share of nude and scantily clad females.

212127.overview: A nice day on the links. Described generously as Sensible Golf without the speeches or graphic detail.

212133.overview: A game inspired by Sid Meyer's Pirates in many ways.  Sail the seas, keep your crew rum happy and fed and with a nice pile of coin or die trying.

212201.overview: Rescue hostages and shoot down alien UFO's in this space-scrolling-shoot em up.

212202.overview:
Well here we have PeeBee, Created using Shoot ’em Up Construction Kit (SEUCK), by Fez Productions

You are a Bee, and you have to shoot various enemies, ranging from Guns at the side of the screen, Little Blue Birds what just hover in position, and Birds what fly towards you

Pick up Dollar Signs, Shoot through Barricades all while avoiding the flying enemies, and Shooting Guns what appear at the Left or Right of the Screen

After a while, You get a Level Select screen, where you are then put into another level, with different scenery, such as Grass and Trees, Snowy Scenes and Sky Scenes, and enemies to shoot away at such as Butterflies, Blobs and Flowers and even Tomatoes what Bounce down the Pathways towards you

This is a well made Game, it plays well, has good sound effects, and should appeal to a wide audience, due to its different levels and visually pleasing effects

212203.overview: In this freeware game by Semtam Softver, you become the commander of a special Paytlik attack unit. Under your command, you will have one to four Paytlíkes, armed just right.

212204.overview: A puzzle game created by Ben Crows/Opaque in 1997. It is a color matching game where groups of 3 drop into the play area, you can move them around to try to best get groups of 3 that will disappear. If you fill the play area to the top the game is over.

212205.overview: A puzzle game in the style of most others, you've got four areas filled with a random assortment of colored shapes. Each area can carry 4x4 shapes. The middle area is empty, except for your little Moper, which can only move around in the center area. By pressing fire while pointing at a shape, the shape will be sucked into the Moper and pushed into another area. Sort all the shapes by color in vertical or horizontal rows. Pushing one shape into another will destroy them. The author's notes identify him as the sole developer and NC Gamez as the publisher.

212206.overview: Preludium is an educational game with arcade elements. The game takes place in the land called Chochland. Krzysztof's goal is reaching the stone with orthographic puzzle. The correct answer to the three tasks opens the door to the next room. The correct spelling indicated at the bottom of the screen needs to be selected from two different choices by using the left or right cursor keys and pressing the fire button. Incorrect answers and contact with obstacles takes one energy level. Topping energy withdraws the players of the two chambers. Arcade part of the game requires a jump over obstacles and avoidance of hostile creatures.

212219.overview: Pallukat is a strange little game in which you play Pac-Man, but instead of chasing and eating the ghosts around a maze, you have to shoot and kill them in what can only be described as a very basic, but fun arena shooter with rather simplistic graphics.

212220.overview: A simple platform game from Park Productions, released in 2000. The game was heavily inspired by the 8-bit classic Chuckie Egg, although it doesn't have the bird in the cage.

212221.overview: Golf game created by Park Productions in 1998 and released as part of the Park Productions Amiga Game Pack.

212222.overview: According to the author, David  Meny, this was inspired by Super Mario Bros. Players control peter on his quest through 20 levels in which he much collect hearts to save his girlfriend Daphne. Extensive jump-and-run game. Your girlfriend has to be saved from various monsters.

212223.overview: PillMania is a Dr. Mario clone for the Commodore Amiga. It was developed and published in 1994 by Focus Design.

212224.overview: A Pipe Dream clone. Each level of this abstract puzzler challenges the player to set up a network of pipes to allow an unspecified substance to flow through as many of those as possible. The pieces are offered in random order, and there are seven different types - straight lines going horizontally or vertically, corners rotating in each of the four directions, and cross-over pieces which carry the liquid straight across horizontally and vertically. Each of these can be entered from either side. When the liquid hits a gap or a piece that the previous piece can't flow into, the pipe is finished.

212225.overview: When pigs fly! Well,they'll fly right now! Navigate your flying pig to get the colored bubbles and avoid the nasties. When you get the requested colors (top left) you move on to the next item in your progress chart. When done they make a picture! Unscramble to letters associated with the picture you drew to move on.

212227.overview: Each level is a maze to be navigated through while fighting off hordes of aliens. Navigate the space station as a lone marine shooting alien creatures and collecting keys, health packs and ammo.

212501.overview:
Little Noah (Petit Noé) is not a game strictly speaking, since it cannot be won or lost. In fact, in this work, intentionally Noah does not die. Rather, Little Noah is all of the experiences Noah has had so far. This is the experience of little Noah. Only this. 
 
It begins in Mom's womb, in her gestation process. Your own heart is beating. He has nine months to train and mature. Weeks are completed when Noah (the “player”) accepts commands that appear on screen (using the joystick up, down, left, or right). But something happens, the bacteria start to appear without Noah being able to do anything to avoid them. At a specific moment, Noah must leave the womb because the infection is not bearable. To do this, you need to press the joystick several times until it is born. Noah starts crying. The game proceeds to a period in the incubator where you learn to breathe and play with objects around you.  
 
The game continues throughout several stages of life and updates progress to add more to the game as time passes.

212503.overview: An AMOS freeware Pac-Man game clone by Anthony Brice, this was his second game ever after a Ping Pong game and the first version was created in about 38 days. With version 1.1 finished and released in August of 1993 according to his notes. 1.10 finished and uploaded to 17Bit Public Domain Library (disk number 2665) in September of 1994. In this version, when you eat a power-pill you can go much faster!

212504.overview: A home-brew Pac-Man game by Churchill Software and coded by Simon Chruchill in 1996. It features an oversized feeling cast of caracters, but all seem familiar. The power pellets that allow you to eat the ghosts are not marked, but are always in the corners, per usual. Clear all the dots to move to the next level and the next song.

212515.overview: Released in the Greek magazine Pixel and on coverdisks for several Amiga magazines. This tile matching game is like Taipei or certain mahjongg variants except it uses all images with no numbers or characters.  The game has many new additions to the traditional mahjongg game, including different board layouts, customizable tile sets.

212731.overview: An unofficial sequel to the wildly popular Pengo game in it your first mission is at The North Pole. You arrive on the day of the annual Pengo-festival for lost penguins. Make your way through 5 maps of pure Pengo-action at the arcades to win yourself an exotic trip to Northern Sweden! Good luck!! In Pengo 2, you must defeat the enemy by pushing ice blocks together to crush them. You also can capture one if they are shocked and dizzy. There is also a time limit to make it a bit more difficult.

212736.overview: A game written entirely in Blitz BASIC. Take part in this maze game. Shoot bad guys and collect various items. Game supports Amiga 4-button joystick.

212754.overview: Bounce the balls against the walls in the correct manner to align the colours and destroy the blocks.

212756.overview:
Plubz is a puzzle game from NC Gamez released in 1997.

The game requires you to pull a colour to create chains and place the pulled colour back to create more.  Each individual level has it's own score.

212760.overview: A commercially released puzzle game by Harald Müller (Mueller) released for English and German speaking players in 1995.

212761.overview: Work to get the pets home in time!

212781.overview:
Pitfall 2 The Lost Caverns, is a fully working and completable port of the C64 release, created using the Scorpion Engine, and graphics are mostly from the Sega arcade version. You play Pitfall Harry searching for the Raj diamond, his niece Rhonda, her cat Quickclaw and a variety of treasures somewhere in the Andes. Poisonous frogs, eels, scorpions, bats, and other hazards get in the way.

Pitfall II is the sequel to Pitfall!, the original platform game. Gameplay has remained pretty much the same, with each screen presenting a side view of obstacles to get past, and potentially treasures to collect. The landscape is more maze-like, with a variety of paths and dead ends to search. Along the way, there are checkpoints the player will encounter in the form of red crosses. When the player dies, Pitfall Harry will be sent back to the most recently crossed checkpoint. The score is reduced based on the distance traveled to get to the cross.

As he explores Harry can collect gold bars which give him a 5000 points award. His total score acts as an energy reserve. If the score is reduced to zero then the game ends and the player must restart from the beginning.

212787.overview:
Peg-it was created by Paul Burkey and released in 1994.  It's a peg solitaire style puzzle game.
PegIt is in many ways inspired by the board game Peg Solitaire. Each level in the game represents a board. You start each level with a number of PegIts. The objective is to remove all but one PegIt from the board. This is done by moving one PegIt over another which is removed. The amount of moves (or jumps as they are called) is limited so you will fail if you make any unnecessary jumps. The PegIts can jump in four direction and must jump over one space. The can't land on top of each others.

To make the game a little bit more difficult, some boards features different objects. Some of these are: Blockers, which can't be jumped over, Trampolines, which allows you to make more than one jump at a time, Teleports and Bombs.

212789.overview: PlayPac is a Pac-Man clone which I started to write because I wanted to learn how to program my Amiga. At the first it was supposed to be just a simple project but, thanks to people who sent mail to me, I've decided to keep the project going on and on. It has configurable size of maze, allows adding tunnels, setting number of Pacs (lives) and Ghosts, turning blackouts on and off and setting game speed and even changing the aggressiveness of the ghosts. Additional settings can be modified to give your Pac a shield, autostarting and saving high scores and tons of other treats.

212802.overview: A maze game  where you have to collect items and avoid baddies.This game by Mike Wellman was released in 1991.

212804.overview:
Like it's predecessor, the unofficial sequel to Paradroid is a top view shoot-em-up set aboard large space freighters filled with droids. After going through a storm in space, the rays affected the droids and they malfunctioned and killed the crew.

You now have to destroy all the droids on the fleet of ships. You control an "Influence Device" which can temporarily control other droids and use their weapons to destroy the others. When your power is low or your damage is high, you will need to transfer to another droid or risk losing your Influence Device.

212805.overview: Pac Man clone by  Kari Pihkala released in Assassins PD Games Volume 16. The game supports one and two player play and even a cooperate mode where players work together to clear the board. A Pac-Man clone for the Amiga, with bold, smoothly moving graphics. The gameplay is basically identical with the original (albeit not down to level layouts or the behaviour of the individual ghosts). The game can be played with joysticks, mouse or keyboard, and by two players simultaneously.

212806.overview: This is a Pac-Man clone released in 1990 by Brainstarr, with only a single level to play it is well done, but too short. In some cases this was used as a cracktro loading game to play while waiting for your main game to finish loading.

212808.overview:
4 Different scenarios, new toys, sweets, caves and forests. 5 levels in each scenario. Updated sound and much smoother scrolling. Pati is a little girl and she loves Abentuer, fun and pre-alto-early lollipop. Today she had a long day, but now it's time to go to bed. Pati also went to sleep, but your adventure was not yet finished, on the contrary, it just started. Pati started dreaming. She dreamed of many things collecting ice cream and sweets in her room or looking for jewels in a cave. But in her last dream, Pati wanted to prove that she is a heroine and that she is strong and now the leader comes for the player....

In a forest you can find yourself as a player, equipped with lollipops and the urge to collect everything you can find. But that's not that easy, because evil Mönsters do not make your goal an easy thing. But if the first time they got some lollipops, they are quickly quiet. 

Published in Amiga Format Issue No: 116 which came out on September 29, 1998.

212810.overview: A multiplayer quiz game where you compete against each other and when you answer a question correctly a square on the board is removed and you get to guess the phrase or celeb pic in the background, a bit like catchphrase.

212812.overview:
Poker Mania, a casino video-poker style game a Reel Poker recreation was created by Andy Green of Green Lizard Productions and released in 1995. It is  a poker variant of a fruit machine simulator. Including all aspects of poker, great playability and the frustration of real gambling. Don't weep as you lose your money, or smile too much as you use your skill and composure to win a bucket load of dosh.

You start off with a few quid and must build your bank to £100 or over in order to progress to Pontoon.

212813.overview: An educational experience on gambling. Playing Pot Fun for an hour or two will cure your desire to go to a live gambling hall. Save your money and get all the fun! Coverdisk for Amigo magazine (Computec Verlag) in 1991.  	Released 1992-08-07 on Amigo! issue 1992-04.

212814.overview: Coded in AMOS. Originally released as shareware, later released to public domain.  A 25 level Tetris clone created by VISUALconcept and released in 1994.

212815.overview:
Official game readme file by Bryan Black:
 Picture this: Saturday night, pub`s closed, nowhere to play darts and drink lots of brown booze.  But not booze for t` baby. Solution: Play Pub Darts!! and hence forth bequeath supreme knowledge through Jimmy Nail`s Adidas bag.  From this bag shall reach an arm that shall reach up the central aisle and from this hand shall reach two fingers, one with the face of Jimmy Saville and the other hence begat  Jimmy Hill, this finger shall reach forth and touch someone on the forehead and he shall be the new messiah who will forthwith give birth....

212816.overview:
Gives you the opportunity to guide one of ten top Premiership sides to the Premier Sixes Cup. One club will ask you to take over the running of their club's squad and you have to guide them to the top. Players such as Owen, Yorke, Shearer, etc, will be at your disposal however it's up to you to pick the right team. Spread over an eighteen week period you must try and shuffle your squad around to ensure that they stay fresh for the run in. 

Versions of this game continued until 1999 with updated players and rosters. The exciting Championship Manager-style match sequences complement the managerial side nicely, together with enough tactical options to make the user feel he is really doing something

212820.overview:
Once upon a time there was a king who had three sons. The eldest was known as Kenneth the Brave. The second was known as Corin the Strong. The youngest was known as the Kevin the Clever. The princes also had a sister known as Gwendolyn the Beautiful. Now in those days there were a lot of evil sorcerers running around and kidnapping princesses and sisters. Gwendolyn, being both a princess and a sister was naturally a target. Dulak the Evil, kidnapped the princess and let it be known that there were only 2 ways to get Gwendolyn back, by paying him an insanely large amount of gold or by sending a champion who could pass all of the obstacles in the dungeon.  
 
Kenneth the Brave volunteered immediately, showing his courage. Corin offered to go along but Kevin decided to wait and see what would happen to his brothers. Meanwhile, Gwendolyn, who was brave, strong and clever as well as beautiful escaped from the dungeon by herself, which drove Dulak into such a fit that he accidentally locked himself inside one of his own magical traps. She related how she had seen her brothers Kenneth and Corin, turned into statues as she fled. Kevin decided that he must go to set his brothers free. Kevin, Gwendolyn and the court wizard all worked together to train Kevin before his departure.  
 
You act as Kevin, preparing for his face-off against Dulak in the puzzle pits. Push the pylon's to the blue spaces, it gets harder as you go.

212835.overview:
The fourth in the series of bat and ball brick breakers. This NC Gamez game version is still different from the others because the racket that allows you to throw and recover the balls is double: there is one on each side of the screen, one on the right and the other on the left. There are small bonuses/penalties that fall when certain bricks are destroyed (slowdown, laser, multiball, next level, etc.). To increase the difficulty, Polataa has bricks on which you have to tap two or three times to make them disappear.

On the production side, the game has beautiful graphics (the bricks are quite big), the sound effects are well chosen and the music is catchy. The game comes with a level editor that will allow, in an extremely simple way, to create new tables.

212836.overview:
The atoms of Earth got pissed off, because the humans wouldn't stop cleaving them to extract energy. So those little, round and jolly things mutated into dangerous macho-macro-atoms (mamas). The atoms didn't realize though what a totally stupid move that was; all of  sudden ANY man with a saw -or a hammer- could cleave the jolly things and build nukeys. 
Your mission, as an excellent world rescuer, is to dismutate all mamas, and as you may have guessed, the only way to do that is with a bat and ball. 
 
The world is counting on you!
 
A bat and ball Breakout\Arkanoid type game with some puzzle elements. Released on Assassins CD4 disk. Game contained a built in editor.

212838.overview: Want to play the ponies? You start the game with £10,000 and through various options: betting, selling or buying horses and making and taking loans you can make a ton! Lots of horses, jockeys, courses to check, distances and conditions to take into account. High strategy for short riders.

213432.overview: Pong50 is an Amiga Pong Clone by Giuseppe Mignogna created to celebrate the 50th  Anniversary of Atari Pong. It is for one player, allows putting spin on the ball and allows the introduction of glitches to gameplay if desired.

213436.overview: A supercharged Q-Bert or Pogo Joe published in the Amiga Power 9 (January 1992) coverdisk 9b, created in 1991 by William Bell.

213628.overview: Protector takes the idea from Defender: the player is controlling a ship over a horizontally scrolling landscape, able to fly to the left and right with different speed. Some residents of the planet are standing on the floor, with alien ships trying to kidnap them. The player has to prevent that by destroying all the enemy ships first. This can be done with the laser cannon or smart-bombs. If all enemies in a level are destroyed the level is finished. A radar helps to keep track of the enemies in the level.

214098.overview: Pacboy is a Pac-Man variant. This version of the concept differs from the original one in the maze layout which is more complex with some dead ends for the player to get trapped in. Other than that the game plays the same with the task of the player to collect all the dots in the maze while staying away from the chasing ghosts. Any contact will lead to a life being lost but by picking up special power dots located in the corners the player is able to go after and kill the ghosts for a short while. Once all dots have been collected the player moves on to the next level which has faster moving ghosts. When out of all lives the player's name can be entered for a high score.

214142.overview:
Pinball I.Q. is an Educational game based on mathematics.
It was published by MicroED and released in Europe in 1987.

214146.overview:
Planet Probe is an Educational game featuring a series of mini-games based on the subject of Astronomy.
It was developed by Paul Falstad and published by MicroED, which was released in Europe in 1987.

214417.overview: A shareware game, written with AMOS, made by Bryan Turnock of Paradize Software and released in 1993. The game is a cross between Pac-Man and Tetris.

214418.overview: Pacman! is a simple version of the classic munching game for the Commodore Amiga. Written as a test project in Blitz Basic, it was never finished. The game archive contains the full source code and the tools used to fetch the graphics from the .IFF files. There is one level of pacman action at three difficulty levels.

214419.overview:
A freeware puzzle game where you must collect all the items in an area, however once you head in a direction, you will keep going until you hit a wall or a reflector item. Now you must discover how to get all items with these limitations and then get to the exit to the next level. This game had a sequel.
A logic game released as freeware and created mainly by one person - Zelený - under the banner of the Crazy Boys group. The game Pacomix is ​​a combination of two well-known games. Atomix puzzle games (where you move atoms and try to assemble a molecule.

214423.overview: A Pac-Man clone by Marcus (Mark) Whitehead, published as freeware in 1989. It has been a part of many PD compilations such as the Assassins, where it was listed as one of the top 10 Assassins games and released as ASI Games volume 102 along with Fruit Salad and Rebound and the Amiga charityware collection called Now That's What I Call Games Disk.

214424.overview: PacWar is a "Pacman" style game with a 2 player difference pitting a Pac player verses a Ghost player.  Lots of nice little bonuses to be picked up by players/ghosts. Game created by Killian Breslin and Mark Brady of Active Software. The demo contains 10 levels, the full version has 50 levels, bonus levels and a subgame.

214425.overview: It's the old pick a pair card game, created by Coagulus Software and released as freeware PD in 1990. It would later be ported to the PC.

214426.overview: Translating to Mr. Wolf or Lord Wolf, this Czech text game was a mix of text adventure with elements of RPG. It is a relatively short and simple game, but with a perfect atmosphere. The plot is loosely set in the world of Middle-earth, and basically it's about some long-forgotten powerful wizard storing his magical energy in a necklace and a ring.

214427.overview: The creator's first game coding in Amos. A logical board game to complete a given pattern. A good cpu opponent and a replay option of the last played game. Published on Fred Fish AmigaLibDisk Fish 600.

214428.overview: A German language freeware breakout clone action game by Felix Wente, written in C and released in 1989. Game came with built in level editor.

214429.overview: A public domain remake of the classic Parcheesi board game by Xavier Egusquiza and released in 1993.

214430.overview: A collection of 20 solitaire card games created by David Smith and released in 2000.

214431.overview: A solitaire game from prolific Mr.  Harald Müller (Mueller), the first of three in a series all similarly named as Patience II and Patience III.

214432.overview: The middle child in the patience card solitaire trilogy created by Harald Müller (Mueller), this one released in 1993, with Patience I a precursor and Patience III the sequel to this game.

214433.overview: The final entry in the patience solitaire card game trilogy being preceeded by Patience I and Patience II. Arrange the cards in the correct order in order to get to all the available cards showing.

214434.overview: Pesten is a Dutch card strategy game from Patrick G. Giesbergen that was released in 1995. It may have been a remake\clone of a 1991 DOS game of the same name. It is known to America and Canada as Uno, with some differences. The object is to get rid of all your cards before the computer opponent can. The game is over when a player has no cards left or if one player has more than 22 cards. Jokers are left in the deck. A Joker can be played at any time except when opponent has just played a 2, it is like a Draw-5 card. There are 3 Jokers in the game deck. You can play a two it is a Draw-2 card equivalent, but if your opponent has a two they can pile it on to make it a Draw-4 back to you! Playing an 8 is like a reverse, play comes back to you.

214435.overview: P-GWIN is an arcade game for up to two players. The action takes place on a single board, where the player must remove designated number of red ice cubes. Some of the cubes hiding a snowball inside. After a while the snowball turns into a hostile snowman. The snowman may be defeated by pushing an ice cube. Contact with the snowball means a loss of life.

214436.overview: A single player, picture puzzle game by Peter Wheatstone, released in 1987 as part of the Amiga Power Pack compilation of games, where, in the latest versions, you can set the number of puzzle pieces, if it is a timed game. If horizontal and vertical flips are required to solve the puzzle, change or turn off music. You can pick and add to available pictures to choose from. It was later released with improvements to public domain in 1992 or 1994.

214467.overview: A German language puzzle game created by puzzlemaster Harald Müller (Mueller). In this one use the available shapes to fill the configuration in question. You can move and reorient the shapes as long as all spaces are taken you can move on to the next level.

214469.overview: Originally unreleased, the Lost Table which is believed to be a pre-production demo that later went on to become the Ignition Table. The original copy was 'found' by stainy and then 'fixed' by StingRay.

214470.overview: A homebrew Pipemania clone with many improvements to the original including ( info from the authors) better graphics, ability to delete a piece that has been laid. 3 levels of difficulty and can quit to desktop.

214471.overview:
Pirates Bounty is a role playing adventure game set in the Caribbean. You are to invade the islands, pillage the towns and build up a Pirate Army. This game is in early access, and will feature more maps and an more elaborate story.

This game is for the Commodore Amiga 1200. It was developed in AMOS Professional 2.00, on a Real Commodore Amiga 1200 for the PTBOGameJam 04, during the 32 hours Game Jam, then polished during the week afterwards.

This game can be played in an Amiga Emulator or on an actual Amiga.

214472.overview: It's mathematical, it's puzzley, but most of all it's fun to play. Use special skills to thwart the computer or another human being! Except Crol Vorderman. It was on the cover of the coverdisk, Issue 59 Disk 2 of Amiga Power in 1995.

214473.overview: A two player, shareware, board game where each player gets to alternately set one of his stones on the board until the last field is occupied. The goal of the game is to enclose as many of the stones of the opponent as possible.

214477.overview: Poker Solitaire is a board\strategy game, developed and published commercially by UnSane Creations, which was released in 1990.

214478.overview: Your objective in this game is to bring the barrels back to the black fields. Game also known as Slider and had slightly different game screen.

214479.overview:
A pool game by M. Vahle, T. Vahle and P. Vahle, relased in 1987. To play, aim the cue ball by moving the mouse. The cute ball will go in the direction of the line radiating from the cute ball and will have a velocity proportional to its length. Click left mouse button to shoot. After all the balls are sunk or the cue ball is scratched, press left mouse button to continue. Click outside the table to end. 
Released on Software 2000 Vol1 Set2.

214480.overview: Time is running low and there are so many popcorn kernels yet to go! You must gather them all in order to move to the next level. Make sure to avoid the fish! Basically Pacman, but with a vertically-scrolling isometric-perspective maze, only one enemy per stage, no power pills, but many other bonuses and bonus systems. Also: Really garish graphics! Would it have killed me to use a more desaturated palette?

214481.overview: In Power Poker you pick your hand and try to beat the computer. Published in Compute!'s Amiga Resource - Volume 2, Number 1 (1990-02). The magazine describes it as: One of the most addictive games we've seen.

214482.overview: Move all the balls on the board from the red starting spots to the blue end spots, you can manipulate the rotating pieces to make a route for them that will take them all home in order to move to the next level. In the course of the action, some squares you cross may blow up, making it harder to get the remaining spheres to their homes.

214483.overview: A clone of Vital Light by Harald Müller (Muller) released in 1994. It was part of the Gamers' Delight and Gamers' Delight 2 compilations. You have 5 colors on your palette, use those colors to make the falling blocks all the same color, which will remove them from the sky. Each level brings more complex mixes and faster falling stones.

214485.overview: A Tetris clone from Harald Müller (Mueller) commercially released by several publishers and released in 1995.

214486.overview: Compete for eight different championship cups including 1993 English or European trophies, Premier Champions, European Cup, FA Cup, League Cup, UEFA Cup or even the Cup Winners Cup in this soccer management simulation written by Malcolm Howard of The Midnight Oil. Define your players, manage and your team and coach. Play at many different difficulty levels for the most fun fantasy football available.

214487.overview: Project Buzz Bar combines gameplay elements from Asteroids and Defender. On each level there are several men to rescue by flying over them. They float loose in space amongst different types of enemy ships, many of which fire at you. Your ship is constantly moving due to a strong gravitational pull from the planet's surface, making it harder to direct the ship at first. The game is written in Blitz BASIC 2, and not only is the source code provided, it scrolls through it on the title screen. The game was released as a coverdisk on The One magazine.

214488.overview: A professional style pub poker game with statistics created by Christian Warren and released in 1992.

214489.overview: There are two versions of this shareware puzzle game by A-Heart Software creators Luigi Recanatese, Stefano Tamascelli and Riccardo Santato. One a 10 level demo\preview version and a full version with many more levels.

214490.overview: Pushem is a game that requires a lot of creativity and creativity from the players requires forward thinking.  The player must, if he wants to solve levels, PUSH red balls onto target squares.  At the same time he can just push ONE ball. A level is considered solved when every target field is occupied by a ball. Another nice sliding game from the 'Sokoban'- Genre for many hours of fun.The game came with a built in level editor.

214491.overview: A Soko Ban style 2D puzzler commercially released by the infamous Courbois Software publishing house.

214492.overview: Two versions of this puzzle game by William Martin exist, as shareware there is the demo version limited to one player against the computer and the full version that allows up to 4 players. Each pyramid has 4 colors, some can repeat. You must play each pyramid into the current game board so that it matches up to the pieces around it. This gets increasingly difficult as the board slowly fills with pieces, all needing to match up on all 4 sides.

214673.overview: A single player video poker game also known as Power Poker and created by Harald Müller (Mueller) and released in 1995.

214779.overview:
A Nintendo Game & Watch style game presentation by Gibs and released in 2012. Amiga Parachute is a Game & Watch simulator. Catch the airborne rangers before they hit the drink or the sharks will get them. Features:

    * Game A & Game B
    * Demo mode
    * Viral Chiptune Music

1.01 : shift digits of the clock for a better display.

214898.overview: Quest is a game from Electric Black Sheep, it is an an 8-way scrolling  top down fantasy shooter with a very nice audio-visuals released in 2021. A map-editor will be available with Project Horizon giving you the opportunity to create new maps for the game, which uses standard  ABK (gfx or sound bank) used in AMOS and the ability to add new graphics, to create a whole new shooter game if you wish.

214921.overview: A homebrew Dart's game created by Paul Whitehead in the AMOS development environment. It was released as freeware in 1992.

214937.overview: A Pac-Man style arcade game created by Dirk Hoffman of Magic Arts and released n 1989. PacMan variant with level editor, many different levels and some new game elements.

214938.overview: A very strange version of Pong with fun power ups! A remake of the classic pong with talking, changing faces, a big flashy score boards, multiple balls and digital sound effects. Poing II: The search for Poing I is for one or two players.

214939.overview: A game based on the board game Perfection where you put shapes into the shapes box as quickly as you can, before the time runs out or else POP!!. Play solo and see how quickly you can place all the shapes, or challenge friends and family by taking turns to see how long it takes you to place the shapes. There are three different levels of difficulty, 9 shapes, 25 shapes and 72 shapes. There are 3 different timers with A being longest and C shortest.

214941.overview: The sequel to Football Masters, this football management simulation game had many interations, all commercially sold by ESP Software and coded by Simon Rush. The last known and most popular release was version 5.08 in 1994. Data disks for different years including the 96/97 season.

214943.overview: A 20 tile scramble of a scene that you must slide to fix, like a 15 puzzle with a few more squares. Released November 25, 2017 by Pozo at the Capacitor 2017 Game Competition.

215013.overview:
A variation on the basic Breakout theme of having a bat at one end of the screen, using it to direct a ball into hitting each of a grid of blocks. In this adaptation the game is unusually played from left to right. Your task is not to eliminate every block, but to gain access to the back wall, by removing the blocks in front of it, and hit it 10 times, at which point you can go through it onto the next screen.

Sets of 8 screens are grouped together, and when you lose the ball on that level you get hurtled back through the previous ones (an idea seemingly taken from the MSX game Break In) at high speed. If you manage to catch the ball on one of them, you can continue from that level, trying to force the ball back through the end of the level, and get back to where you were.

On each level, the value of the different colours of blocks varies - the points schedule is listed a the side of the screen. Some blocks score onto your bonus rather than directly, others require multiple hits to be removed, and most sets of blocks will regenerate once all are removed - which gives you a chance to increase your score, and also adds points to your bonus.

The levels also contain a variety of bonus bricks, which are revealed as you remove the blocks on top of them and must be hit again to activate. These include bonus multipliers, extra balls, transformations to the ball's physics, and extra lives. There are 5 skill levels, and 2 players can play alternately.

215046.overview: An updated version of 1993's Logik also by Harald Muller. Like the original it is a great thinking and combination game for the whole family. You have to try to recreate a heap of diamonds according to certain rules of the game, which must match the original both in shape and colour. On each level you also play against the clock and have to try to solve the puzzle as quickly as possible.

215047.overview: A playable demo futuristic pool type game from Darren McKie, released in 1995. Ricochet around and hit all the locations of the bumpers that match your color. The bumpers will stay in place, there are no pockets in this game until the very end, just trying to hit all your locations before your opponent does. If you hit one of your pegs a second time it will light back up. When you have hit all your pegs\bumpers a hole will open, sink your ball and you win!

215082.overview: A set of Mods for Gloom entitled either Gloom Mod Map or Plenty of New Maps, which is just that with content from nittamituaki, AmigaFans, FirstAge, Plenty1, Plenty2, Plenty3 and a IDO-CD32 compilation.

215114.overview: The Prophet is the next generation in R.P.G.s. It features over 200,000 locations with over 50 different location types. There is no set route through the game. Discover plots within plots. Help the poor or just kill for money and power. Quests that change the shape of the game. Completing one may open or close another. A unique learning system. A full graphical display of your character showing the different armour worn and weapons held. There's dozens of different items - Keys, food, potions and spells and a multitude of terrifying monsters to face. This game really has what all you RPG addicts have been waiting for.

215138.overview:
Premier Picks is an unusual card game based around football (soccer). The game takes the form of a 'season' of variable length involving the 20 real-life Premier League teams of the time (name can be edited, but displayed kits can't). Players pick one of the 18 visible cards, to dictate the result of the match.

There are several different types of cards in the game - your overall aim is to get more goal cards than the opposition. The other cards include free kicks (which give you another pick), substitutions (which replace that card with another), and penalties (in which you have to run the pointer across the screen, clicking on as many cards as possible - you have a few seconds to find a goal card). The game is split into 2 halves, and each of those has a card which immediately ends the half.

Before each half there's a 'card reveal' feature, which, depending on when you click to stop the pointer, reveals between 1 and 6 cards. This has numerous tactical implications, and is the main skill aspect in the game.

215139.overview: A spartan video poker game created by MicroSys and released in 1992.

215140.overview:
Game concept & design by Bryan Styer and pilot Capt. Earl Rogers. Coding by Steve Michel. PRECISION APPROACH: JET INSTRUMENT TRAINER was intended to be a simulation tool rather than a game that allowed commercial pilots to develop/maintain proficiency in flying aeroplanes. Additionally, it allowed pilots experienced in other aircraft to become familiar with Boeing 727 operating techniques, which form the basis of the flight simulator.

PRECISION APPROACH was exclusively made for the Amiga and originally released in 1989. Enhanced 512K and 1MB versions followed in 1990. The 1MB version was only made available to customers upon request, who were required to send in their original disk with a self-addressed stamped envelope to the publisher.

215141.overview: 1941: Japanese airplanes are attacking Pearl Harbor on Hawaii. You are an US soldier and must defend the port with your ack ack gun.

215142.overview: A single player Boulder Dash, or Repton style game created by Francis and Raymond Irving, that features a very unique and interesting appearance. The different objects in the game work and hang together well. There's a built in level editor, making it fun to create new levels. Plasma Bubble was written using GFA Basic.

215143.overview:
The aim is to bring water at the end of the pipeline. The water slowly fills the pipeline. The major issue is that enemies (tools and mice) can create holes in the pipepline. To fix holes, you have to reach one of the blue collar men (touch him). He will then follow you. Bring him to the hole and he will fix it. You will need to protect him from the enemies because otherwise he will be killed and you have to bring him again (as he will re-appear).
You can have the two men with you instead of just one. Once the water has reached the end, you need to bring a blue collar men to the end of the pipeline (there is a sort of valve and I think he opens it). Then you and the two men will take a victory posture and go the the next level. Unlike most pipeline style games this one is setup up more as a platformer than an puzzle\action game.

215144.overview:
Paris-Dakar is a rally simulator in which the player controls a wide variety of variables, including the state of the car (gasoline, water, damages, gear box...) and the race route (always accessible), among others. If needed, the player can refuel, buy water or whatever else is required from the powerboats in Europe or the tankers in Africa. Prices of these essential materials aren't always very reasonable, given the player's meagre starting wallet, motivating players to earn higher sponsorships through strong performance in the race.

There are three different stages: one in Europe, another one in the desert of the Sahara, and finally a crossing of the Tenere desert before arriving in Dakar.

215152.overview: Written for the Light & Phenomena Easter Party, 17th to the 20th April, 1992 in Alingsås and as part of the Game Pack 1 on  Phenomena and Light Easter Conference 1992. The game is a single player, tile matching puzzle game based on the Tingstu source.

215228.overview: A playable demo of the Amiga incarnation of the Nintendo Game & Watch Popeye game by D.I.E.D. and released in 1989.  Catch the cans of spinach and don't let Brutus get them, keep up your strength.

215276.overview: You play as Captain Caveman in a harsh desert environment where you must jump, bash and avoid all manner of creatures, from stinging ants to camels and rhinoceroses and even Aladdin himself in order to pick up the caches of coins hidden here and there.

215323.overview:
A dungeon crawler for one or two players from Zsoft for the Amiga. Not much to say other than it seems to be built on the same engine and principles as their other games as well as the Black Dawn series. Coded, music and gfx by Shaun Watters (timeslip1974), graphics by Timothy Jon Gilbert
Musician : Mike Richmond. This game had a sequel in Parasite II.

215324.overview:
A really good and cute looking puzzle platformer.

You play as a fox and the aim is to get the penguins to the exit by using switches and stuff (similar to Lemmings but still not). The blue penguin can pickup and use keys and red one kill baddies. It is a precursor to Bograts: The Puzzling Misadventure.

215535.overview:
Project Horizon is an 8-way scrolling  top down shooter sci-fi game for Commodore  AMIGA. 
The player is a NASA astronaut on the Moon (1977 - alternate timeline) who is find himself in a war situation.

216741.overview:
Puppy Love is an early example of a virtual pet simulator. The player becomes the owner of a puppy that has just been rescued from life in a junkyard. The puppy dreams of winning ribbons and trophies at a dog show and it's the player's task to train it up to do so.

When starting out the puppy will run around the player's front yard and doing tricks on its own. After it has done a specific action the player can press the spacebar and name it. When the name thereafter is typed in the puppy will attempt to do it again. The player can then reward the puppy for doing it right by giving it a bone and it will then eventually learn it. When a few tricks have been learned it is possible to create choreographed routines. This is done through a built in programming language using simple English sentences where the player types in plain text which tricks each routine should contain and how they should be performed.

After learning some tricks and routines the puppy can enter the competition of a dog show which is made up of ten events. The first three involve doing specific tricks while the next six involve doing choreographed routines in competition with other dogs. After winning all nine the puppy is allowed to compete in the final and most challenging event. To make the puppy do tricks or routines the player simply types in their names but it can only perform tricks that it has practised at home.

216758.overview: A public domain release from The Assassins that contained Jumping Jack, Technoball and Zillo. These compilations were sold by mail order through a number of suppliers of public domain software who would usually assign their own catalogue number, so it is not uncommon to find the same compilation on offer from multiple suppliers in the same magazine, usually for a fairly nominal fee above the cost of the disk and copying labor.

217300.overview:
Powermanga is an arcade 2D shoot-em-up game with 41 levels and more than 200
sprites. It runs in 320x200 or 640x400 pixels, with Window mode or full screen and
support for 8, 15, 16, 24 and 32 bpp. It was ported to OS4 by Frank Menzel.

217304.overview: Passengers on the Wind II allows players to decide the fate of the heroes and direct all of them so that they reach their aim. Players will discover many locations, directions, and events; and will live different stories according to the directions that he makes the characters take. Everything is controlled using either the keyboard or the joystick.

218089.overview: The sequel to the 2021 Christmas present for the new year! Published in the Amiga Addict issue 17 as the cover disk. Use the Gift-o-matic 5000 to make sure the right presents go to the right homes. No more shooting every present into the chimneys!

218163.overview: Can you help Santa deliver all his presents in time? Avoid the rooftops and shoot those presents into the chimneys and pick up treats for your reindeer along the way, which will give you extra time. Avoid the tempting sherry if you want to go fast, it will slow the game down....though slowing down at Christmas time isn't always a bad thing.

218421.overview:
An unofficial port put out for the 30th anniversary of the original Pinball Dreams release by Tukinem's using Blitz 2. This unofficial port includes four tables: Neptune, themed to underwater exploration, Safari, themed to an African safari, Revenge of the Robot Warriors, themed to a battle against robots and Stall turn, themed to aerobatics. For those of you who want to know what's improved in this new update, it has improvements such as better physics, a start screen, table 3 selection and other changes listed below.

    - starting animation of tables when choosing players ( 3 table blinks as in the original )
    - the "ZAP" inscription can be lit when the ball flies under the letters and after all the letters are lit, the bonus lamps at the very top ( x2, x4 etc. )
    - you can slowly earn points in several places
    - we have 3 balls to start, but there is no game over for the player after losing all balls
    - you can choose one player for now during table animation ( F1 )

219287.overview: A puzzle game similar to games like Pipemania for the Commodore Amiga

278873.overview: A Game n Watch LCD style game recreation for the Amiga created by Mike Verstaevel of "Gardening" fame and released to PD in 1998.

418375.overview:
Puzzle slide 
Created by Ze Emulatron from Lee Hurley productions in 2011 use a joystick in port 2 to move the pieces in the puzzle. The tile pieces used in this game were made in deluxe paint iii and can be replaced. They are named t1 image, t2_image etc. There is an example t1 on the disk that is the correct size. The files have to be converted with ifftrans that is from compute's second book of amiga, it has been included as ifftrans.Bas. The palette used in this game is in the file palette_colours. Each line has 3 values, red, green, blue.

418397.overview:
A sequel to the first 6 versions of Poing. The last installment in the Poing series sums up the entire series by combining the latest version of the unorthodox Breakout engine with levels from several of the earlier games as well as third-party level packs.

As usual, in this horizontally oriented Breakout, it is your task to bounce a ball on the right wall. After hitting the wall ten times, it opens and your ball reaches the next level. If you miss the ball, it comes back at a blazing speed through previous levels, giving you at least some kind of chance to pick it up instead of losing it immediately. If the ball is too fast, and your power level too high, which often is the case if the ball has been in play for a long time, it may momentarily destroy your paddle.

There is a plethora of blocks, from the basic ones with varying levels of hardness to those that expand into four blocks, crystals that give bonus points, magnetic blocks, deflecting blocks, pinball-like bumper blocks, holding blocks which temporarily hold your ball and then release it at speed, etcetera. Destroying an entire group of blocks usually makes it reappear in a new guise, with new effects, usually releasing a group of bonus crystals as well. Likewise, there are many bonus blocks such as slow-downs, multi-ball, bonus multipliers, dancing vector bonuses, autopilot, gravity and much more.

418572.overview: An Educational game for children with 4 game types written by Paul Harthen and released by Prisma Software in 1991. The primary game modes are Garden Games, Alphabet Tree, Creepers, Counting Corner and Paint Pot.

418574.overview: Children's educational software focusing on spacial awareness, colors and the joy of creation. Published by Alternative Software in 1996. Color, create and print!

418575.overview:
Based on 1986 Mr Chip Software/Mastertronic C16/Plus 4 release, P.O.D.: PROOF OF DESTRUCTION.. POD was given away free on CU Amiga coverdisk #41 (Sept 1992) and landed them in trouble with the ELSPA. CU Amiga were subsequently banned from including further such conversions on their coverdisks. Gridrunner style gameplay for this top-view budget shooter with 25 levels, challenging you to survive until the time runs out. You start with three lives, but get an extra one (up to a maximum of five) when a level is completed. The time goal is not reset when you lose a life.

You guide a small spacecraft around a screen representing your people's power grid, moving it in the four compass directions along the grid lines. Aliens fire in all directions, so there are no 'safe spots' in which you will not get hit. Their shots cut lines out of the grid, preventing motion along that space for the few seconds it takes to reform. Every fourth level deviates from the norm by simply forcing you to shoot aliens for bonus points. Lives can still be lost during and gained after these

418580.overview: A one or 2 player multi-scrolling space shooter with split screen play created by Matthias Narroschke, Jan Engehausen with graphics by Freddy Emden and Music by Audun Evensen collectively known as the Animators.

418607.overview: In PsychoBlast, a crosshairs shooter from Team Manga and released to PD in 1997, you have to protect a circle in the middle from the onslaught of a large variety of wiggling sprites. Shoot them all before they touch that precious shape!

418739.overview: A sexually explicit text adventure with more than mildly misogynistic themes and some outright racism thrown in with a poorly spelled story, all created by the aptly named Sick Minds Software and unleashed on the world in 1992.

418757.overview:
Projekt Prometheus is a German text adventure with graphics. It is set in 2012 directly after the explosion of a nuclear plant. The only way to get rid of the radioactivity is to fetch a resource only available in space. Unfortunately the whole crew of the space ship was killed by a plague and only one man, a journalist, remains. He has to figure out the space ship controls and solve puzzles, e.g. dealing with a contaminated command console.

The player communicates with the game by typing in commands with the keyboard and reading the game's text descriptions. However, the player can associate often used orders to the function keys. The icon bar, controlled with the mouse, offers additional functions or notifications, e.g. a compass which is used to leave a room, switching between text and graphics (not available for all rooms) or a mini map of the space ship.

418964.overview:
Destination: The ancient Egyptian city of Karnak. Alien forces possessing
horrifying powers have sealed off the once thriving community from all outside
contact. As a covert operations specialist, you have been trained for all
forms of contingencies. Nothing can prepare you, however, for the nightmare
you are about to enter...

420284.overview:
Pengo (68K)
This is a transcode from the original arcade game Z80 to 68K assembly.

420910.overview: Passages is a puzzle game created by Paul Ruane and released as shareware under the name PSR Software in 1994.

420940.overview: Shoot various baddies coming towards you. You must shoot the enemy that is the same colour as you. A shareware puzzle shooter, created with AMOS and released by AIM Design in 1997.

420984.overview:
This is Psychoblast from 1993 by Ordyh Software (This Game was given away with the special version of SEUCK distributed with CU Amiga Magazine) and was otherwise sold as Shareware. 

It is a one screen game, where you remain in the middle of this over-powering blue screen, you remain inside a box and just have to shoot out towards enemies such as Dice and Triangles and other flashing enemies what appear. You have a counter top-left what counts down from 999, and your score is as usual centre bottom of the screen. There are also decent sound effects as well, not a bad Game to play, But quite challenging due to the limited play area you have.

421371.overview: An unfinished playable demo from Johannes Lipp in 1991 who made 3 games with two of them ready for publication and this one in production. When German disk magazines passed on the first two games, Slez and Denjoy, it meant that Pot would never be finished.

421968.overview: Play as the FBI in this adventure\shooter by Av Ragnar Yri and John Everett, published by Courbois Software in 1989. Named Prijs Schieten in the Dutch release.

422244.overview:
This is a German, shareware puzzle adventure set in Egypt and written with Oberon.  There are a lot of mystic riddles which you have to solve. Not for adventure\riddle beginners. Pamehta is also a first-class graphic adventure. It takes you into the mysterious world of ancient Egypt. Quite unprepared, you suddenly find yourself in the middle of the game and have to gradually figure out what it's about. When it becomes apparent that you are suspected of being the thief of a valuable flute, you have to prove everyone wrong. A journey begins through the country on the Nile, which has many surprises in store.

Pamehta has a very comfortable mouse control; the keyboard can be pushed aside straight away. If you click on the “Action” button, the program lists all possible commands at that moment, which in turn can be executed with another click.

Like Evil Tower, Pamehta is written entirely in German and offers a lot of reading material. Together with the beautifully drawn pictures for each location, a great adventure atmosphere is created. This adventure doesn't have to hide from its commercial counterparts either. For the shareware fee of around 12 marks, which is almost ridiculous considering the quality, you get a program that will give you many exciting and entertaining hours.

422248.overview: A two player AMOS freeware game where you must match the pictures using your memory. It was created by Charles Mead and started pairing up with players in 1990.

422254.overview: An AMOS based property management simulation created by Martin Warne and released as freeware in 1990.

422255.overview: Solve the puzzle by matching the picture in the bottom left of the screen. You must slide letters to match. A 1992 shareware AMOS game from N. J. Harris.

422256.overview: A German language strategy game created by Marc Fischlin in 1990 (with version 2.0 coming out a year later). Pythagoras is a trading game where 1-4 players try to qualify as king of their city. It takes place around 550 BC. At the time of the colonization of the Mediterranean region. The player has many options for action: he can trade, distribute lands, fighting wars, levy taxes, plunder towns, buy or sell ships, buy land, etc. Almost the entire game can be controlled with the mouse.

422257.overview: A commercially released horizontally scrolling nautical shooter created by Oscarsoft using the SEUCK engine and released by Pactronics in 1989.

422258.overview: Set up and run your own successful Bingo game in real life. The shareware software allows you to create flyers, betting lines, jackposts, prizes and to present it to a full house and rake in the dough. Released by Dave Brown in 1993.

422271.overview: A Call-Ware text adventure coded by Ventilator of the Big Mac Brothers of Switzerland in 1994 and available in both English and German. You start off in bed with the sun shining savagely into your eyes and the day can definitely go downhill from there.

422274.overview: A freeware AMOS crosshairs shooter game from Thierry Floquet, made in 1998. Splat Bill in the face! Each un-pied Bill makes him stronger so no slacking!

422275.overview:
An Amiga freeware point and click and text adventure game made by Robert Sedler in 1994. The text adventure Psycho Ward is a surreal dark comedy set in a mental institution. The main character is a nameless patient, driven to escape the institution, who seizes their chance by falling down a laundry chute into the basement while the nurses aren't looking.

Psycho Ward was created using the Dream Weaver authoring system (not to be confused with Adobe Dreamweaver). The interface is similar to adventure games produced by Legend Entertainment in the early 1990s such as Spell casting 101 and Eric the Unready, where about a quarter of the screen is used to show the actual game text, then there is a small static picture of the current scene (shown from first-person perspective), and the rest of the screen is filled with helpful GUI gadgets that the player can use instead of manually typing in commands. There are clickable arrows for the main compass directions (and up/down movement), action buttons (look at, take, drop, etc.) along with a list of less-common actions the player might want to try (search, punch, kiss), and two lists of available objects: one for objects in the current room, and one for inventory objects the player is carrying, with a toggle button to switch between them.

422310.overview: A German language pig farming management game from The Game Creators, released as freeware in 1993.

422900.overview: An unfinished Lunar Lander and shooter hybrid style game created using the Infinity Engine, originally created in 1999 and updated in 2020, the game got more difficult at each level with stricter fuel limitations and more difficult terrain and impediments including hostile aliens that you must fight.

422901.overview: Eventually released as a homebrew game, this Robocop inspired shooter came to most people's attention via a playable demo in 1989. The feel of a beat-em up but with scads of bullets flying everywhere. The Robocop project was taken off line after several fundamental errors were discovered during the "Live Situation" tests. OCP Spokesperson said that the project was neither reliable nor effective in certain situations. It has been noted that the biological side was no longer correctly interfacting with the loyalty\command circuits and Robocop had become a liability. Three years later in a joint OCP\military operation, the new edition 209 Mk2 cop was put on the streets and has been put into service. A fully armored, fighting machine to protect the innocent, and serve the public trust of upholding the law. You are ED 209 Mk2 you are.... Pseudo-Cop!

422903.overview: A freeware title by The Silents in 1993. A Snake\Worm game with a twist...or is it a slither? Grab the colored blocks for points there is a way to transfer half your tail to your opponent, find it! Great for parties, use the join in and the score will be reset. When one player is dead the play mode will automatically go back to single player mode until join is used again. When you die you get 10 points per chain.

423086.overview: A Czech language high school dropout text adventure game by Amiga Bestware Company in 1993.

423365.overview: In this first-person muncher created and released as freeware by Andrew Heckles in 1994, you go through Pac-Man's maze at ground level to gobble up all the dots and avoid the ghosts. Good luck, you're going to wish you had someone watching over you.

423390.overview: A horizontally scrolling Uridium style shooter by Paranoid in 1990. Released as freeware and labeled a demo.

423391.overview: An unfinished cartoony beat-em up created by Insert Coin in 1997 where you play the titular Policeman fighting street thugs from the part to the bar.

423393.overview: A one or two player shareware puzzle game in the style of Columns created by Thomas Bachert and released in 1991.

423394.overview: The third edition of the quirky horizontal Breakout clone Poing has undergone great improvements, representing much of what would define the remaining installments in the 7-part series. There are now more upgrade blocks, including some which mainly serve visual purposes, such as dancing polygons in the bottom of the screen. Other additions are sampled drums (while the rest of the music is still real-time synthesized), new algorithmic drum patterns and the intricate star bricks which both increase bonus points, turns on the dancing polygons and make your ball harder so that it can break the "bricky bricks". More levels, more options to play them in a fixed or random order and new power ups!

423395.overview: Poing 5 is an Amiga breakout / pong arcade game released in 1997. The game was developed by Paul van der Valk. The fifth installment in the Poing series comes with a new levels, music and improvements.

423396.overview:
An unreleased 3d Engine intended for doom-like games. Features: Walls, floors, two screen sizes (256x200 and 192x160), doors, animated walls. Poom is reasonably fast on its intended target processor (68020 or better) and the 256x200 version is detailed. The gameplay area is large, with numerous
corridors and functioning doors. It is something of an empty world but was a promising engine at the time.

423397.overview: Powerball is a simple shareware puzzle game where the player must clean each screen from all the coloured bricks. This is possible by using a ball that bounces up and down in the screen and can be controlled by the player who can move it left or right. The game features a staggering 80 levels in 8 worlds including a level editor to add your own levels.

423399.overview: the year is 2049 and boxing, wrestling and karate have all mutated into a single sport. See if you can win and grab the cash in the Prize Fight! Programmed in ASM 68k by Powerhouse, this shareware martial arts game was released in 1992. As shareware there was a freely distributed demo, and you could send in to own and play the full game.

423400.overview: A shareware Tetris clone for your desktop with Beavis and Butthead samples created by Mirage in 1993. Play Tetris to the giggles and grunts of the zany duo.

423415.overview: A freeware game from John Filsak and released in 1991 based on a story told by Jesus. You, Taz, are the Prodigal Son. The plot centers around the younger son who, impatient and greedy, asks his father for his inheritance. The father agrees, but the son wastes his money, eventually becoming homeless and destitute. In the end, to the son's great surprise, he is welcomed back into the family by his father and brother. However, based on your choices, your ending may be different.

423417.overview: A one or two player freeware Pog game by Jean Pierre Software, released in 1996. Flip the pog and get more to play with, fail to flip in time and lose your precious pogger.

423418.overview: In this freeware shooter by Cult in 1990 your mission is to destroy all Bazookabears in the slime. On level one it is a vertically scrolling shooter where you fly to the Slimezone and must avoid Red-Acid-Cloud and can avoid or shoot enemy missiles. On level 2 it is a crosshairs shooter you blast the Bazookabears just aim for thier Bazo for best results.

423419.overview: The very first Czech text adventure book for the Amiga, a rather complicated story of a special agent, a pilot. Created by Straton Software in 1991.

423421.overview: A statistics driven one or two player Premier League game where randomness is driven by a card choosing system that keeps things exciting. An F1 Licenseware game created by Dave King in 1993.

423423.overview: An updated version of the original 2015 game Prisonnier by Off Game in 2020. Based on an old 8 bit game this update added much better graphics and speed.

423424.overview: An AMOS based freeware puzzle game from MAGE software in 1994. This single player 15 puzzle game was dedicated to Anna Bartosiak and challenged you to solve each randomized puzzle in as few moves as possible.

423425.overview: A two player AMOS based freeware game created by Off Game in 2015. Game code is available freely on GitHub, but it is a classic game reworked from 8-bit roots.

423428.overview:
The sixth installment in the Poing series comes with a levelset entirely about mathematics. Bounce you ball, in a horizontal Break Out-style, against bricks building up numbers, mathematical signs and formulas.

Everything from the previous Poings is there; hit the right wall ten times to open the way up to the next level, and if you miss your ball, it comes hurtling back through the previous levels. There is an overwhelming amount of special blocks altering environment and ball physics, graphical effects in every corner, and semi-randomised music.

Apart from the levelset, the game engine has been revised. A new two-player "squash" mode is available. If you don't have a friend to play against, the computer will analyse your skill level and create a balanced drone player for you to spar against. A new "wheel of fortune" block gives you the chance to earn high point values when the ball lands in a trap block. Two other new block types are the teleporter blocks, which transport your ball to another place on the screen, and a block which diverts the ball in a straight line to the left at high speed.

423434.overview:
Fill the 15 pieces and create the picture in this freeware game by Ali T. Ozer of Kronos Digatal in 1987. Put the picture back together from the pieces. To grab a piece, move the mouse over it and click the left button. To rotate a piece (90 degrees CW) first grab it, then click the right button. To see what the full picture looks like, choose the SHOW option from the menu. To see how close you are to the solution, choose the CHECK option.
Many thanks go to: D. John Hodgson (for the small IFF reader), Tom Rokicki (for the bitmap rotations), and Helene (Lee) Taran (for the popup menus & her many suggestions). R.A.F. Spreading Service (Rome) for Mak Soft.

423435.overview: A Polish freeware pub trivia quiz intended to have the questions come from the computer and have viewers answer on paper or by calling it out and then get the answers and scoring from the computer, so the number of users\teams is infinite the way the game is played. The game has difficulty settings, the ability to set sound responses and prompts, record and score keeping and to set up team names and information.

423436.overview: Slide the 19 piece mixed up puzzle to create the full image. A Shareware game created by Delf Schlüter and released in 1993.
