423482.overview: Pingwynne (not to be confused with Pengwyn, Pengo, Pingo, Penguin or Percy Penguin) is a totally new concept in computer games. Pingwynne is in fact SHAREWARE, which means that, if you like it, you are supposed to send me some money (£3 would be nice thankyou). This will of course be channeled back into program development, and not spent on beer or loose women. Guide Pingwynne around the ice maze, avoiding the marauding creatures which are intent on his destruction. Push ice blocks (use FIRE button) to try to crush them. Arrange the special coin blocks so they are touching, and win an extra life. Watch out for vikings, vanishing spirits, Eric the Halibut, etc., and, most terrible of all Pingwynne's evil twin brother Clive...

423488.overview: A Pipe Dream style puzzle game from Amonia, created as freeware in 1991. Construct a large enough network of pipes before the time runs out and the water starts to flow.

423506.overview: A freeware, German language puzzle game from Achim Kern written in ASM 68k in 1994. In each puzzle the player faces a grid containing assorted shapes in some of the cells. Below the grid are outlines of some of the colored shapes that are in the grid. The player's task is to maneuver the shapes in the upper grid and drop them onto the corresponding outlines. The player uses the arrow keys to move a red box around the screen, when this comes up against one of the shapes in the grid the shape will move and will continue to travel in the direction it was pushed until it hits another object or the edge of the game area.

423514.overview: An AMOS based, Czech language, freeware game by Hologram from 1999. A complete remake of the rather strange prehistoric text game ported from the 8-bit Atari.

423592.overview: A two player ping-pong\table tennis game created by Skyhook as a freeware game. The game was part of the 1991 Astronut & Wise Man compilation.

423598.overview: A horizontal Breakout\Arkanoid style game created by Kallasoft to support AGA graphics and released as freeware in 1988.

423679.overview: Peg Puzzle aka Towers was Created by James as freeware in 1990 using ASM 68k. It is a basic Towers of Hanoi puzzle game where the object is to move a pyramid of colored disks from the left peg to one of the other pegs. You may only move one disk at a time, and you may not place a lager piece on top of a smaller one.

423700.overview:
The Treasure of the Golden Suns or Poklad zlatých sluncí is a Czech icon driven game with graphics. The game was programmed by Charon Software in 1992 and distributed by Vochozka.  Poklad Zlatý Sluncí is probably the first original domestic Amiga game sold for money. 

Just like the older Duck Tales(1991) from ZX Spectra, we will take on Uncle Skrblík here . One day he is reading a newspaper and finds an article about a treasure that pirates have hidden somewhere in the Valley of the Golden Suns . However, no one knows where this place is located. It is only known that there is a map for it, where one half is owned by the penguins from the Museum of Colors and will not release it after good. The other half then got lost somewhere. Coincidentally, the nephews are cleaning so frantically in our house that they swing the chandelier in our study, which falls and reveals a roll of paper with the second part of the map. The sight of enormous wealth motivates us to immediately drop everything and go on an adventure.

423701.overview: A Czech language text adventure based on Jára Cimrman's fairy tale Long, Wide and Short-sighted. As Prince Jason, you must overcome the evil giant Kolodej and save Goldilocks from her lost beauty. Created as freeware by Martin Orlický in 2009.

423714.overview: A single player Marble Madness\labyrinth\maze style game written in AmigaBASIC by Top-Soft in 1990. In this game your aim is not to reach the exit, but to collect all the colored squares to complete the level.

423716.overview: Polonista is an educational grammar game in Polish, developed and published by Faterbit, which was released in Europe in 1995. Educational program for learning Polish spelling, designed for primary school students. In addition to a large amount of didactic material, the player has a set of tests at his disposal.

423788.overview: A freeware version of Tetris created by Petri Airio in 1998 that allows multitasking and opens the default screen to match the current resolution on the screen. It was also called Petris '98 or in some cases incorrectly labeled Tetris '98.  To get maximum score drop pieces as soon as possible and do not use next preview. And as usual, the more lines you remove at one time, the more score you will get. If all the horizontal line is one color you will receive a special bonus.

423821.overview: An unreleased horizontally scrolling space shooter created by Fullspeed Creative Development in 1997. On planet Aktris the Tektrons have one of their biggest station of producing Warships, it must be destroyed. 96% of the planet surface is water so keep your ship dry fighting these ocean-based aliens.

423999.overview: Strategy game in the style of "Kaiser". The aim of the game is to build a pyramid. To do this you can buy/sell boats, camels and slaves etc. It is always displayed how far the pyramid is already finished. Created in AmigaBasic by Martin Jochimczyk in 1990.

424288.overview: A crossword game with additional functions to help you with crosswords where you only need to know one letter in any place. Thanks to the library of 76,000 entries, you will solve the crossword in no time.

424369.overview:
A Polish language educational game by Twin Spark Soft in 1994. Pythagoras is the first comprehensive program for learning mathematics. The emphasis in the program is on learning the methodology of solving tasks applicable at subsequent stages of learning. The program can assess a student's results and diagnose his or her achievements. Based on Pythagoras, you can find out your shortcomings in understanding the material in a very clear way. 

Pythagoras has a number of mechanisms that make it impossible to "cheat" the assessment of knowledge of the taught material, which allows this program to be treated as the cheapest but demanding tutor. The professionalism and substantive correctness of the theoretical materials contained in Pythagoras are guaranteed by the authority of their author, a doctor of mathematics from the Jagiellonian University.
During the learning phase, the program asks additional guiding questions and explains the next stages of solving the tasks. You can gradually give up on this help, because the end goal is to solve tasks on your own. Tasks can often be solved in many ways. The tips suggest a method that minimizes the chance of making a mistake. The complete course consists of the following parts (sold as separate programs):
7th and 8th grades of primary school and secondary school exam,
grades 1 and 2 of secondary school.
grades 3 and 4 of secondary school.
Pythagoras is the cheapest tutor!

424677.overview:
Join the journey of a lifetime as you help Alice, a girl stranded in the Pleiades star cluster, find her way back to Earth. 
Navigate through space, gather powerful "ray stones," and unlock the Alcyone space station's engines to guide her home.

449127.overview: This editing system for Premier Manager 3 allows you to edit almost every aspect of the default database. You can change the names and abilities of each player, and transfer them to other teams. You can choose which divisions each club starts in, and can manage any of these, rather than having to start from the Conference league. You can even insert European teams to create a Superleague-type setup. The length of time particular injuries keep a player out for can be changed, as can the points system of the league. Once you've saved the changes and started the edited game, you can load it back into the Multi-Edit System and make further changes.

449191.overview:
Released on Power-Disc issue 3.

Although it looks very similar to it, this is NOT another "ordinary" Tetris clone. There are some additional shapes including a W-like shaped tetromino that don't make life as easy for you as with "normal" Tetris.

449677.overview:
The first and only game using "The Puzzle Gallery" engine, for which there were supposed to be multiple Puzzle Disks. Extremely similar in style to Are We There Yet? and The Fool's Errand, "At the Carnival" includes word searches, jigsaws, block puzzles, word squares, crosswords, jumbles, cryptograms, mazes, and more.

Each puzzle is set at and somewhat related to a different attraction at Hazard Park. There are total of 40 attractions, and 180 puzzles.  
 
The Puzzle Gallery: At The Carnival was originally developed for the Apple Macintosh in 1989. The Amiga conversion was created for Miles Computing. Also published in Amiga Future #134 (coverCD), Sept/Oct 2018, publisher was APC&TCP.

449913.overview: A homebrew fighting game from Axival Software for one or two players, it was released to PD in 1996.

449932.overview: Pro Gammon is a computerized version of the popular board game, Backgammon. It was developed by Kevin Glynn and released into the public domain in 2003.

451587.overview:
Featured games in this compilation:

   •  Zynaps -This horizontally-scrolling shoot 'em up features 16 levels and 450 screens of Nemesis-inspired action. You pilot a spacecraft through the levels, shooting as many of the encroaching meanies and mounted turrets as possible. Power-up tokens are offered for shooting some, which can be used to obtain better weapons including ground-attack lasers, speed ups and multiple bullets. Extra lives are on offer as well, which you'll certainly need, especially as you have to go back a long way when losing a life.

   •  Nebulus-You play a small green guy who needs to blow up eight towers because their presence is somehow poisoning the water of planets which could potentially be ideal colonies. Unfortunately, you need to get to the top of these towers to blow them up. 

    • Exolon-This flick-screen action game combines shoot 'em up and platform elements, as you control a flying man who can gain an exoskeletal suit for extra protection (hence the name). Your task is to progress from left to right in each level, either along the ground or by using the arrangement of platforms. Most of the baddies can be avoided rather than shot, and this is often easier, especially as you can duck or jump to avoid them. As well as a standard gun (activated by tapping fire) you also have a limited number of missiles to take out installations (activated by holding down fire, which makes autofire facilities useless).

    • Netherworld-In this game you are trapped in Netherworld. With your space ship you have to make your way through different levels with a hostile environment. Under a time limit you have to collect diamonds to get to the next level. The game is filled with dragons, moving mines, acid spitting creatures and lots more. Your space ship is able to shoot, furthermore you can collect several power ups, such as sand glasses to ease the time limit, shield restore or items that give you invulnerability.

451867.overview: Hillery and her Liberal friends have taken total control of the world. You are one of some 10 million people left, scheduled for transferring to the country of your origin. But, someone has tampered with your environmental control causing you to awaken from a mind controlled state. Your objective, to learn all you can about Panic Society, escape from your prison, find master control, shut it down, and rebuild society. Panic Society uses the mouse and keyboard. A Multilevel graphic puzzle adventure by 	Ronald F. Picardi in 1995.

456110.overview: Pecos Bill is a Wild West themed 1-2 player co-operative shooter developed by Adolfo Cirillo using the Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit, and released into the public domain in 1996.

456118.overview: Pie Quest is a 1-2 player co-operative shooter made by Ricky Derocher using the Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit, and released into the public domain in 1986.

456292.overview: Bump into enemies to attack them but be careful because some are strong, and some will weaken you to the point that you can't continue.

456361.overview: A winding path cuts through the deep forest, hidden among moss-covered ruins and ancient trees. Legends speak of untold secrets, hidden treasures—and countless dangers. Only the bravest adventurers dare to enter, seeking to uncover the mysteries that lie within.

461841.overview:
"Passatempo" is an AmigaBASIC game that bears a very, *very* faint resemblance to *Space Invaders*. The objective is to prevent the mouse pointer from colliding with various tiles that gradually advance from the bottom of the screen. You will be surprised by the program's small file size.

Published in the November 1988 edition of AmigaMagazine OnDisk #3.

461853.overview: Press Fire PONG for Commodore AMIGA 500 isn’t just another Pong clone, it’s a reimagined arcade experience with unique gameplay mechanics and dynamic visual effects. Unlike traditional Pong, in this version, you must move the paddle up or down in a different way:  Hold FIRE → paddle moves up, Release FIRE → paddle moves down

461935.overview:
Pool is a highly realistic simulation of a billiard table. It allows you to play any type of billiard game, featuring ball movements that are far more true-to-life than those found in any other program of its kind. The extra time the program takes to calculate ball trajectories is offset by its exceptionally high level of simulation.

To launch Pool, double-click the icon. You will be presented with a screen showing the billiard table and various controls.

If you check the menus, you will see that you are in Practice Mode.

To shoot the cue ball, click on it and—without releasing the mouse button—move the cursor across the playing surface; a straight line will appear, indicating the direction in which the ball will travel.

Published in Amiga Magazine OnDisk #22 in April of 1991.

461987.overview: Published in the October 1997 issue of AmigaMagazine OnDisk #93. One of the final issues.

465498.overview: This is a version to improve the graphics of the Amiga Police Quest III game. The palette has been optimised and some graphics have been improved. Created by the SCP group.

465502.overview: Pooperino is a small single screen platformer where you collect coins to free your family that was taken by an evil wizard.

470011.overview: As dark omens spread across the land, demons stir in the depths, preparing to invade the world of men. While kingdoms remain unaware, one wizard senses the coming doom.

471342.overview: Popspin is a Puzzle Bobble/Bust-a-Move clone that was developed and released by Pin at Revision 2026.

481706.overview: This game is an adaptation of the Italian adventure Morgan Tyler: Star Plague by Bonaventura Di Bello. It was originally written using The Quill and Illustrator and published by Edizioni Hobby S.r.l. on the cover tape of Viking, no. 4, April 1987 for the ZX Spectrum and Commodore 64.

481728.overview: After more than thirty years, ghostly lights are dancing over Bardach Castle once again. Only the legendary knight Zyndram of Białków can save the land — and the one sent to find him is Dratewka the shoemaker, who is busy squandering his ducats at The Dead Goat tavern.

481871.overview: POLE POSITION - Amiga AGA & ECS version

482015.overview:
Pi-game – Amiga 500 Edition

A simple but addictive survival game brought to the Commodore Amiga 500!

Pi-game – Amiga Edition is a port of the original JavaScript/HTML5 game created by Peter Norton for the web.

The concept is easy to understand, but surviving for a long time is another matter! You control the π (Pi) symbol inside a circle that gradually fills up. Your objective is to keep moving, avoid being trapped and survive for as long as possible.

482087.overview:
After having defeated the evil Grand Vizier Jaffar, the brave Prince claimed just one reward: the hand of the beautiful daughter of the Persian Sultan. However, as the Prince approached the palace, his appearance suddenly turned into that of a beggar. Someone who looked just like the Prince ordered to throw him out. It turns out that Jaffar is alive and back for vengeance. Banished from the palace, the unfortunately Prince must travel to faraway lands and find a way to defeat the villain.

Prince of Persia 2 is, like its predecessor, a cinematic platformer. Much of the gameplay is reminiscent of the first game, focusing on precise jumping puzzles, swordfighting, and overcoming many hazards in order to stay alive. Swordfighting is more prominent and features situations where several enemies attack the Prince at once. Reinforcements may arrive after the Prince has eliminated all visible enemies. Like its predecessor, the game must be completed within a time limit.

482117.overview:
PITFALL! REMASTERED for the Amiga
Based on Activision's Pitfall! (Atari 2600, 1982, David Crane)
Amiga remaster by TjLaZer 2026

482122.overview: P.O.W. is the second light-gun game for the Commodore Amiga similar in style to Operation Wolf. The premise is to rescue a group of trapped US soldiers from hostile territory.

482173.overview: PITFALL II: LOST CAVERNS - REMASTERED for the Amiga Based on Activision's Pitfall II: Lost Caverns (Atari 2600, 1984,David Crane)

482177.overview:
This is the first game from the neogeo hardware/taito system B ported to the Amiga 1200 !
A native 680X0 assembly port, designed to take advantage of the AGA chipset and the Amiga 1200’s stock processor.

482281.overview: A first-level demo of my ongoing AGA enhancement of Prehistorik, originally released by Titus in 1991

482580.overview: This a game for the Amiga 1200 based on the Quickbasic Gorillas.bas game and combined it with a bit of Pooyan. It was made using Amiblitz 3.

482589.overview: In 1985, VEB Polytechnik in Karl-Marx-Stadt built Poly-Play, the only slot machine ever manufactured in the GDR: a case, a coin slot and eight games to choose from.

482811.overview: So we have fond memories of Punchy on the Commodore 16 and decided to port it to the Amiga. During that process, I discovered that there were actually quite a few different versions of Punchy out there, so I thought, why not make a collection of them?

482820.overview: The Amiga never faded away. Nintendo looked at Commodore’s wedge-shaped wonder, with its copper and its blitter and its four channels of glorious Paula sound, and thought: “Yes. That one.” Gaming magazines ran cover stories about the deal, and kids begged for an A1200 for Christmas because the box had a Pikachu on it.

482903.overview: The Game Boy Color edition, in full GBC colour, with Pikachu following you around and Pikachu’s real voice played as a sample through Paula. Yellow is the biggest of the four, so it needs an A1200 with fast RAM. Loading takes about 50 seconds while the disk unpacks itself. Think of it as Pikachu getting comfortable in its new Poké Ball.
